name: @jojo/service
description: The shared layer: the knowledge graph, its tools, and the React binding. Imported by web and mobile, owned by neither.
//exports: Seven entries, one per layer, each a star whose TARGET names the extension.
That last detail is the whole reason a map is viable at all, and it cost two
probes to find. Metro does not extension-probe THROUGH an exports star, so
`"./*": "./kg/*"` fails to resolve `@jojo/service/core/model` on the phone;
it does resolve a star whose target already ends in `.ts`. Vite, tsc 6.0 and
tsc 5.9 accept both spellings, so the browser side cannot tell you which one
is right. One character, four resolvers.
No `conditions` object, ever. `expo/tsconfig.base` sets `customConditions:
["react-native"]`; bare string targets make that inert, and the moment a
conditions object appears, mobile's tsc and Metro resolve through the
`react-native` condition while web's tsc does not. That divergence has no
error message.
No barrels. `export *` from a `kg/core/index.ts` blinds layerOf() in
check-layers.mjs, and Metro's minifier tree-shakes less than Rollup's, so a
core barrel would drag statistics.ts into every React Native screen. A
per-file star buys the same spelling with none of that.
Adding or renaming a layer is a manual edit to this map. There is no error
until bundle time if you forget. The same goes for the two exact keys under
`./react/`: a star target names ONE extension, and `kg.tsx` and `status.tsx`
are the only two files in the package that render, so they are listed by
hand ahead of the star. An exact key wins over a pattern in every resolver
here. Write a third .tsx and it will not resolve until it is listed too.
//source: No build step, and no `main`. Both apps compile the TypeScript themselves — Vite for web, Metro plus babel-preset-expo for mobile — and web's kg compiled clean under mobile's older tsc at full strictness before any of this moved, which is what made shipping source rather than output safe to choose. `npm -w @jojo/service exec tsc -b` is the authority on whether it type-checks; the apps' own programs also pull this source in through their imports, but they do it under their own lib and types settings and without types/portable-globals.d.ts, so that pass is incidental and must not be treated as the check.

scripts.lint: oxlint kg && node scripts/check-layers.mjs && node scripts/check-platform.mjs && node scripts/check-no-copies.mjs
